fields.title: Polka: the database that is running out
fields.summary: 6.8 TB out of an 8 TB limit and growing at 340 GB per month. Headroom is three and a half months.
fields.decisionPrompt: What do we do this sprint? Name the cost of your decision.
fields.brief/role: You are the Polka product manager.
fields.brief/company: Polka is a fictional local grocery delivery service: 900 partner stores, buyer app, and partner dashboard.
fields.brief/context: Polka's main database takes 6.8 TB with a server limit of 8 TB. Growth is 340 GB per month and accelerating: 180 stores connected over the quarter, three more chains in negotiations. Headroom is about three and a half months. A solution is needed for the upcoming sprint.
fields.brief/objective: Free up enough space before server failure without postponing the problem for a year.
fields.brief/constraints: Three and a half months of headroom. Solution needed this sprint, single team.
fields.brief/task: Decide what to do this sprint and justify it.
fields.learnTakeaway/title: Space doesn't run out everywhere equally
fields.learnTakeaway/body: Before buying a server, look at the composition and age of data: usually half is taken by what is almost never accessed. Retention solves two tasks at once — space and deletion obligations — and costs weeks, not months. A bigger machine buys a year and returns the same problem more expensively, and sharding requires choosing a key before you understand how the product grows.
fields.evidenceCards/0/content: Order items 4.1 TB, orders 1.2 TB, analytics events 0.9 TB, catalog and stock 0.4 TB, other 0.2 TB.
fields.evidenceCards/1/content: Orders older than two years make up 47% of volume. Accesses to them over the quarter: 0.3% of all reads.
fields.evidenceCards/2/content: "Options: switch to a server twice as large — two weeks, plus 180k/month, buys a year. Partition and move old data to archive — three weeks, saves about 45%. Shard — from three months, solves it long-term, but the key must be chosen now."
fields.evidenceCards/3/content: Personal data in orders older than three years must be deleted — requirement set half a year ago, unfulfilled.
fields.decisionOptions/0/description: Server twice as large. Two weeks, +180k/month. One year headroom.
fields.decisionOptions/0/consequence: fast, reliable, requires no product decisions. The problem is postponed, not solved, and will repeat in a worse form in a year. Legal requirement remains unfulfilled.
fields.decisionOptions/1/description: Three weeks. Orders by month, older than two years to archive storage, older than three are anonymized.
fields.decisionOptions/1/consequence: frees up about 45%, i.e., 3 TB. Headroom — about a year and a half. Fulfills legal requirement. Product change: history in the dashboard becomes "two years", older — on request with a delay. Affects 0.6% of users.
fields.decisionOptions/2/description: Three to four months. Solves capacity question long-term.
fields.decisionOptions/2/consequence: will not make it in time — headroom is three and a half months, timeline coincides with failure moment. Partner dashboard becomes cross-shard and requires migration to analytical storage. Key is chosen now and hardly changes.
fields.decisionOptions/3/label: Move analytics events to separate storage
fields.decisionOptions/3/description: Move analytics events to separate storage. A week and a half. Frees up 0.9 TB.
fields.decisionOptions/3/consequence: fast and substantively correct — events don't belong in the product database. But 0.9 TB is two and a half months of growth. Doesn't solve, only delays.
fields.rubric/remediation/0/gap: Does not distinguish between partitioning and sharding
fields.rubric/remediation/1/gap: Does not distinguish between partitioning and sharding
fields.rubric/remediation/2/gap: Did not link retention period to capacity and cost
fields.rubric/remediation/3/gap: Failed to see that analytics events do not belong in the product database
